newsitem.title: USA: Ohio House backs school fiscal and academic reform.
newsitem.headline: Ohio House backs school fiscal and academic reform.

text.p: The Ohio House early Thursday approved plans requiring greater fiscal and academic accountability for the state's public schools.

The measures included as part of the planned overhaul of Ohio's school funding system required a simple majority from representatives, said Cheryl Burchard, spokeswoman for House Speaker Jo Ann Davidson, R-Reynoldsburg.
The accountability package already approved by senators would require school districts to create "rainy day" funds and budget forecasts five years into the future.
House Finance Committee members are scheduled to begin tackling proposals approved by the Senate to pay for the court-ordered reforms later Thursday, Burchard said.

A task force appointed by Gov. George Voinovich has recommended increasing the state sales tax to provide $1.1 billion of revenues annually to finance the school plan. The task force also recommended $5.8 billion of bonds for school construction over 10 years.

The Senate plan includes the sales tax increase, a property tax increase on businesses and a property tax cut for individuals making the net increase less than the $1.1 billion the task force recommended.

The sales tax increase, general obligation bond authorization and permission to allow school districts to seek real estate tax increases that would grow with property values all require constitutional amendments approved by voters.
Lawmakers must approve constitutional amendments by a 60 percent majority. They have until August 6 to approve amendments if the referendum questions are to be placed on the November ballot.
